blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.
blocks.zh: 视频生成正在从端到端的合成转向代理生成,其中规划,工具使用和反馈可以实现连贯,可控制的多镜头视频. 与此同时,视频世界模型提供有行动条件的观测和预测未来,作为代理商的互动环境. 我们通过代理工具来研究它们的相交点:一个可执行的运行时间,构建上下文,曝光工具,保持状态,路径反馈,并管理围绕视频模型的预算. 本报告审查了三个方向。 首先,制作代理视频,在这些系统中协调脚本、拍摄规划、资产管理、制作和编辑,同时应对这些系统的评价挑战。 第二,代理世界建模,利用调解观测、控制、执行和状态。 我们讨论了游戏引擎或代理写作程序在视频模型提供观测时维持世界状态的混合设计,以及代理和世界模型如何相互评价和改进. 第三,视频模型开发中的递归自改进(RSI),区分出输出修改,更新来利用状态,生成参数,以及评价者,以及改进程序本身的变化. 我们确定这些改进如何反馈到以后的发展之中。 在这些方向上,我们分析必要的代理能力,包括视听感知、长视距规划、记忆、基于代码的互动、反馈指导控制、技能再利用和多代理协调。 最后,我们在自主视频制作、终身记忆、可编程混合控制、自主模式开发、出处、成本核算和评价方面面临挑战,将视频质量和任务业绩与持续改进模式和利用联系起来。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: 1.1 Motivation
blocks.zh: 1.1 动机

blocks.en:
Video generators produce increasingly realistic, controllable, and temporally
coherent clips [ kong2024hunyuanvideo ] . A generator alone, however, does
not organize the decisions needed to complete a video task. A creative brief
must become coherent shots;
references must persist across scenes; takes must be inspected; edits must
preserve what is correct [ huang2026vimax , vista2025 ] . Interactive
video must also support continuing actions grounded in observations, not
just a finished clip [ gao2026lingbotworld2 ] .
These requirements motivate a transition from video generation
to agentic video generation: a goal-directed process in which generated results
inform subsequent decisions. An agent can revise a plan, retrieve a reference,
select a tool, or localize a failure in response to actual outcomes [ li2026videogenagent ] .
Agentic video generation denotes a system-level perspective, not a new generator
architecture: the video model provides synthesis or predicted transitions,
while the agent makes consequential choices around those capabilities.
Video couples these choices over time. References affect later shots [ chen2026cinecrew ] ,
actions change subsequent observations, and local repairs can disrupt
temporal consistency elsewhere. Plausible footage may still violate a
narrative requirement or fail to realize an intended action, so a quality
score alone rarely specifies what to do next [ liu2024videogenerationevaluation , ding2026playworld ] . Effective control
requires connecting observations to localized decisions while maintaining
project or interaction state and accounting for generation cost.

blocks.en:
The development from large language models (LLMs) to agents offers a
foundation for this control. Rather than only generating a response, an
LLM can operate within a cycle of reasoning, tool use, and observation,
as demonstrated by ReAct [ yao2023react ] . Planning and memory extend
this cycle to tasks requiring multiple decisions [ weng2023agents ] .
Making these capabilities operational requires an agent harness:
the executable runtime around the model that constructs its context,
exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and enforces permissions
and budgets [ weng2026harness , ning2026code ] (Section ).
For video generation, the harness is where a creative brief or an
interactive goal becomes executable operations on generators, editors,
and world models. The central question shifts from generating a good
clip to reliably completing a video
task through feedback. Agentic video generation and video world-model interaction are two
concrete settings. A further question is whether experience from these tasks
can improve the system that will perform future tasks.

blocks.en:
Feedback changes different objects at different timescales. Prompt revision
or take replacement targets the current artifact [ vista2025 ] ;
retaining a skill targets subsequent tasks [ wei2026videoweaver ] ;
updating a dataset, critic, or generator targets later model
versions [ liu2025videoalign ] . These outcomes
should not be conflated: effective repair of a current video does not by
itself establish improvement in future capability.
Beyond repairing individual outputs, context engineering considers
how instructions, retrieved evidence, memory, and execution records are
selected and organized for subsequent decisions [ weng2026harness ] .
Agentic Context Engineering (ACE), for example, accumulates and revises a
structured context from execution feedback rather than updating model
weights [ zhang2025ace ] . Such work shifts attention from a current
response toward reusable knowledge, while leaving open whether the
mechanisms that construct and update that knowledge can themselves improve.

blocks.en:
Recent work on automated research extends these ideas to model
development. The AI Scientist links idea generation, coding, experiments,
and reporting [ lu2024aiscientist ] ; autoresearch runs a bounded
loop of training code modification, experimentation, and validation-based
acceptance [ karpathy2026autoresearch ] . These workflows connect proposals
to empirical feedback, but automating a fixed experiment loop is not the
same as improving the loop itself. Research on self-improving agents,
exemplified by the Darwin Gödel Machine and Regularized Recursive
Self-Improvement (RRSI), explores changes to the
agent’s own code or harness [ zhang2025dgm , xia2026rrsi ] .
Such work motivates examining the processes that generate and validate
subsequent improvements.

blocks.en:
Recursive self-improvement (RSI) asks whether a system can improve
the procedures that produce further improvements [ chen2026surveyr04 , duan2026surveyn21 ] .
Video-specific targets include failure diagnosis, data collection,
supervision construction, update
selection, and candidate validation. Repeating a fixed collection-and-training
pipeline is iterative improvement. The recursive direction additionally
allows evidence to revise that pipeline, changing how a later round discovers
and addresses weaknesses.
An agent harness provides an executable surface for this direction.
Its context construction, tool orchestration, memory, testing
workflow, and update-selection rules can be inspected and, where authorized,
revised [ weng2026harness ] . This does not make every harness
self-improving: a revision must be retained and independently evaluated on
later tasks or improvement rounds under stated resource constraints [ xia2026rrsi ] .

blocks.en:
Existing video research supplies parts of this connection: feedback can
revise reusable production skills [ wei2026videoweaver ] , uncertainty can
guide data acquisition for adaptation [ savov2025autoexplore ] , and
validation can govern critic renewal for later training [ yang2026dualipo ] . These are
building blocks rather than evidence that one system has completed the full
RSI loop. Our survey therefore connects three questions: how harnesses
organize agentic video generation, how they support video world-model interaction,
and how they may drive video-generation development toward RSI. The first
two establish task execution and sources of experience; the third examines
persistent capability and the procedures used to improve it.
Figure 2 maps representative work from a shared video
generation foundation into the three directions corresponding to the questions
below.

blocks.en: 1.2 Contributions and Positioning
blocks.zh: 1.2 捐款和定位

blocks.en:
The survey addresses three questions about the influence of the agent harness
on video generation (Figure 1 ), each corresponding to
one core chapter.
blocks.zh:

视频生成(图1),各对应

blocks.en:
How does the agent harness enable agentic video generation? Agentic Video Generation (Section ) studies
how harnesses coordinate planning, execution, tool use, memory, editing, and
watermarking around shared project state, and what the evaluation of such
systems must separate. We examine how feedback changes
generation and editing decisions and how those changes affect video quality, consistency,
and efficiency.

代理机如何带动代理视频生成?. 代理视频生成(部分)研究
如何利用协调规划、执行、工具使用、内存、编辑和
围绕共享项目状态标出水分,以及评估此类状况
系统必须分开。 我们研究反馈如何改变
生成和编辑决定,以及这些变化如何影响视频质量、一致性,
与效率。

blocks.en:
How can the agent harness be integrated into video
world models? Agentic World Modeling
(Section ) locates where a harness can intervene in
observation, control, execution, event organization, and state management,
and examines designs in which an engine holds the world state
while the video model renders it.
We examine how these interventions support sustained interaction, control
fidelity, state continuity, and agent-driven evaluation. The focus of this
question is how a harness enables reliable interaction with a video world
model.

blocks.en:
How can video generation systems move toward recursive self-improvement? Toward RSI in Video Generation
(Section ) examines how advances in video
generators and the agent harness can feed back into the process that produces
subsequent model improvements. We review foundation model improvement,
agent harness improvement, and evaluation, and identify the channels through
which gains in these components can strengthen failure diagnosis, data
curation, training, and validation in later development rounds. The goal is to identify mechanisms
and evidence needed for recursively improving development processes that
can support next-generation video generation models.

These questions connect through feedback: agentic video generation and world interaction

blocks.en: Differentiating Our Work from Existing Surveys
blocks.zh: 将我们的工作与现有调查区分开来

blocks.en:
Existing surveys provide complementary accounts of video generation.
Work on spatiotemporal consistency examines generation models,
representations, training strategies, and evaluation, emphasizing the
mechanisms that maintain coherent video sequences [ yin2025spatiotemporal ] .
Post-training and alignment surveys organize methods for adapting video
generators to human intent, including supervised fine-tuning, distillation,
preference optimization, and inference-time adaptation [ li2026videoposttraining ] .
Evaluation surveys examine perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and
alignment with user instructions [ liu2024videogenerationevaluation ] .
Together, these accounts explain how video models are built, improved,
and assessed.

blocks.en:
More directly related to our system perspective, agentic visual generation
surveys organize the conditioning, execution, and adaptation decisions
available to a controller across visual modalities [ huang2026agenticvisual ] ,
or study autonomous multimodal content creation and the construction of
stateful artifacts [ xu2026ags , wang2026artifactcreation ] . Wu et al. place agentic generation and world-modeling generation on a single
capability ladder of visual generation [ wu2026visualnewera ] .
World model surveys characterize predictive and simulation capabilities
across domains, focus on action conditioning, memory, and responsiveness
in sustained interaction [ chu2026agenticworldmodel , liu2026interactiveworldmodel ] ,
or treat world models as interactive proxies that supply feedback to
continually improving agents [ yang2026quovadis ] .
Harness surveys analyze the execution layer around text and coding
agents [ ning2026code , guo2026harnessdesign ] .
Surveys of self-evolving agents and RSI examine evolutionary targets,
adaptation stages, and feedback loops across general AI
systems [ gao2025surveyr02 , chen2026surveyr04 , wu2026rsisurvey ] .
These perspectives share concepts such as feedback, memory, and agent
control, but none of them takes the harness around a video generator as the
unit of analysis across production, interaction, and model development.

blocks.en:
Table 1.2 compares related surveys and
adjacent studies by scope, thematic coverage (including RSI), and agent design.
Our survey complements these perspectives with a framework centered on
video generation that covers three settings in which a harness meets a video
model: as a synthesizer in production, as an interactive environment, and as
the object of development. The settings are linked through the harness:
agents organize generation and refinement, while video models provide
interactive experience that can inform agent decisions and further model
development. Where capability ladders treat agentic
generation and world modeling as successive stages of the

blocks.en:
Our contributions are threefold. • A harness-centered framework. We define a common agent–harness
execution loop (Section ) and apply it to
production, organized by workflow function
(Section ), and to world-model interaction,
organized by the interfaces through which a harness intervenes,
including designs in which an engine or a program holds the world
state (Section ). • An account of improvement. We separate revisions of the current
output from updates to harness state, generator parameters, and
evaluators, and from changes to the development procedure. We identify four channels
through which an improvement could re-enter video development.
No surveyed system yet revises the procedure that trains and
validates the generator (Section ). • Evaluation requirements and open problems. We state how the agent harness
supports active testing and reciprocal evaluation of agents and
world models (Section ), what the
evaluation of agentic production must separate
(Section ),
which capabilities video imposes on agents
(Section ), and which challenges remain
(Section ).
